chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:
“The thief is not to have his hand cut off until he confesses to the theft twice. If he retracts, he remains liable for the theft, but his hand is not cut off, when there are no witnesses.”
And he said: “The fornicator is not stoned until he confesses four times when there are no witnesses. If he retracts, he is left alone and is not stoned.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ: four separate confessions required in this case
key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the act of theft for which liability is established
key_terms.شُهُودٌ: witnesses whose testimony could establish the offense
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: the prescribed stoning punishment is carried out
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the prescribed amputation is carried out

ai.seo_question: How many times must a thief or fornicator confess before hadd punishment is carried out in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning the evidentiary standard for applying the hadd punishment in theft and zina when witnesses are absent. It distinguishes between establishing liability through repeated confession and the effect of retraction, which prevents the hadd punishment while leaving financial liability in theft.
